author: misilva73
content:
<@372317178906542081> , you can find the analysis [here](https://github.com/misilva73/evm-gas-repricings/blob/main/notebooks/5.1-eip-6780-same-tx-create-selfdestruct.ipynb). I used Xatu data to get it.

What you are asking is changing the spec of 8037. This would mean making a new release for the spec and adding new tests, all clients updating their code, redoing all the backward compatibility analysis and warning affected entities again and relaunching the public devnet for testing with the new spec. This would mean the fork is delayed, plus all the coordination cost to the ecosystem.

Even ignoring the fact that adding refills for 8037 is not the right solution (and means moving in the wrong direction for SELFDESTRUCT), delaying the fork for this use-case is not worth it in my opinion. I am not convinced by the argument of things will be too expensive and folks will move to move centralized venues. Base fees are expected to do down that will alleviate the cost increase. In addition, the usage of this pattern is very small to warant the costs I described above.

author: misilva73
content: If you feel strongly about this, you need to make sure the EIPs you care about are in the proper shape for the Hegota headliner discussion - without a strong champion, the likelihood of not being included is low.

author: misilva73
content: This won't hapen by itself as it requires works and focus

author: gaxanh
content: I believe that the low adoption rate stems from the fact that the network did not initially encourage this model, rather than the other way around

author: misilva73
content: But that is exactly why the right solution is not to put a temporary bandaid on `SELFDESTRUCT`, but instead work on making `TCREATE`, `TSTORE` and `TLOAD` work. From what I seeing, this is where you guys should put your energy on (specially if you want to see them included in Hegota), instead of arguing for charging 8037 so late in the process.
